back: Used to describe a sudden event in a story.
An expression of surprise when meeting someone in an unexpected place.
Ironic comment when someone says something they think is true but isn't.
Used to say that you strongly agree with someone.

front: I'll believe it when I see it
back: Expressing doubt about a future event.

front: to cut a long story short
back: Used when skipping the details of a story to get to the point.
Used to describe a fortunate or unfortunate coincidence.
Used when something sounds simple but is difficult to achieve.

front: it's not the end of the world
back: Used to comfort someone by saying a situation isn't that bad.
Stronger way of saying 'I don't know'.
Used to emphasize that you do not have certain information.

front: the fact of the matter is
back: Used to introduce the most important part of a situation.

front: it's just one of those things
back: Used to say that an event happened without a clear reason.
Expression of surprise at learning something new.
